newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London up, Dow seen mixed to higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London up, Dow seen mixed to higher.

text.p: U.S. shares were slightly firmer in London following Wall Street's late sell-off on Monday. Trading volumes were light as European investors remained wary of a possible sharp downside correction for U.S. blue chips.
"Wall Street had a big fall late in the session which may have been a bit overdone," one dealer said. "We could see the Dow start a bit better today but the market is still looking vulnerable."
On Monday, the Dow industrials closed down 36.52 points at 6,268.335, triggered by profit-taking in high-technology issues, dealers said.
The Dow has fallen a net 113 points, or 1.7 percent, in the past week and 338 points, or 5.1 percent, since reaching an all-time peak of 6,606.3 on November 26.
Overall market pessimism was reinforced by news that Morgan Stanley had recommended reducing share holdings.
The U.S. investment bank changed its global asset allocation to 56 percent stocks, 29 percent bonds and 15 percent cash versus and original 74 percent stock and 26 percent bonds bias.
"Morgan Stanley is just the latest to change its portfolio bias towards cash and bonds. It won't be the last," another dealer said.

High-technology stocks, which took a hammering in New York overnight were generally firmer. Intel, which lost $5-1/8 on Monday, was up $3/8 at $127-5/8 while Digital rose $1/4 to $38-1/4. Dow Chemical was up $1/8 at $79-1/4 after its chief executive officer, William Stavropoulos said in Singapore on Tuesday that analysts forecasts of steady earnings for the company in the fourth quarter were "pretty accurate".
The March S&P 500 futures contract traded on the Globex after-hours futures market, was up 1.75 points at 729.50 by 1105 GMT.
